Slice: Check Out Tool

Step 1 of 12 in Borrow and return a tool · the story starts here · before Tool Inventory — tool checked out · State Change

Intent

Let a neighbor borrow a tool, self-service, from the Tool Catalog. The checkout opens a loan with a due date set from the tool's default checkout period, or from a shorter period the neighbor chooses. It is also how a holder collects a tool set aside for them: there is no separate pickup command. The checkout records only Tool Checked Out; the hold's end is recorded by the Hold Collector (Collect Hold), which reacts to the checkout.

Trigger & Actor

The neighbor who will borrow the tool, from the Tool Catalog screen, on a tool the catalog offers Check Out on (available, reserved or set aside). The shed manager does not record checkouts. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.

Command / Input

Command: Check Out Tool

A LoanId, ToolId or NeighborId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's checkedOutAt is that same moment.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
loanIdLoanIdyesA UUID chosen by the caller for the new loan, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different loan already recorded (INV-CHK-12).
toolIdToolIdyesThe tool to borrow. Must be a tool that has been added (INV-CHK-11).
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor borrowing it, who must be the one making the request (INV-CHK-1). Must be a registered account (INV-CHK-11).
loanPeriodDaysIntnoOptional. Whole days, from 1 up to the tool's default checkout period (INV-CHK-6). When absent, the default applies. A fractional value is refused, never rounded.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Catalog @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Checked Out → context Loans Read by: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog and My Loans; Holds To Fulfill (the tool is out); Overdue Loans To Notify (the loan's due date); Holds To Collect (the borrower's hold on the tool, if any, is now collected).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
loanIdLoanIdyesFrom the command. Identifies the loan everywhere from here on.
toolIdToolIdyesFrom the command.
toolNameTextyesSet by the system: the tool's name as recorded by Tool Added, copied so the loan's readers never look it up.
neighborIdNeighborIdyesFrom the command: the borrower.
neighborNameTextyesSet by the system: the borrower's name as recorded by Neighbor Registered.
neighborEmailTextyesSet by the system: the borrower's email current at checkout (Neighbor Registered, replaced by any Neighbor Email Changed). Readers that email later keep the address current themselves.
loanPeriodDaysIntyesThe period the loan started with: loanPeriodDays from the command, or the tool's default checkout period when it was absent.
dueDateDateyesSet by the system: the checkout date (today) plus loanPeriodDays. A later Loan Extended sets a new dueDate; this one never changes.
checkedOutAtInstantyesSet by the system: the UTC moment of the clock reading above. Its date in the shed's local time zone is the checkout date.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Checked Out changes the tool's entry in Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog, starts the loan's entry in My Loans, and puts the borrower's hold on the tool, if any, on Holds To Collect for the Hold Collector. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-CHK-1: A neighbor checks a tool out themselves, for themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId, and the request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch otherwise). The shed manager does not record checkouts. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in, before anything else is checked.
  • INV-CHK-2: A tool that is already checked out can't be checked out again until it is returned or recorded lost.
    • A loan is open from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan.
  • INV-CHK-3: A tool set aside for a holder can be checked out only by that holder, until the end of the collect-by date.
    • A tool is set aside from Hold Fulfilled for a hold until that hold ends. The collect-by date is Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate, recorded on the event; this slice reads it and never works it out.
    • The holder's pickup is an ordinary checkout. There is no separate pickup event.
  • INV-CHK-3a: A tool that is back in the shed with holds waiting, and not set aside, can be checked out only by the neighbor whose hold is at the front of the queue.
    • This holds after a return before Hold Fulfilled is recorded, and after a set-aside ends before the next hold is fulfilled.
    • The front of the queue is the hold on the tool, still waiting, whose Hold Placed was recorded first. Queue order is the order the Hold Placed events were recorded, never a comparison of times.
  • INV-CHK-3b: A holder's claim on a set-aside tool ends at the start of the day after the collect-by date, shed local time, whether or not Hold Expired has been recorded yet.
    • From that moment the set-aside is treated as ended. If a hold is waiting, only the neighbor at the front of the queue can check the tool out (INV-CHK-3a), and the former holder is refused. If none is waiting, anyone can, the former holder included.
  • INV-CHK-4: A retired tool can't be checked out.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that, so it can't be checked out either.
  • INV-CHK-5: A neighbor with an overdue loan can't check out a tool.
    • A loan is overdue from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, while it is still open. The due date is the latest one set by Tool Checked Out or Loan Extended. Nothing records it; it is worked out from the due date and today.
    • Any open loan counts, including one whose tool has since been retired. A loan that ended because the tool was recorded lost no longer counts.
    • This also stops a holder collecting a tool set aside for them.
  • INV-CHK-6: The due date is set at checkout: the checkout date plus the loan period.
    • The loan period is the tool's default checkout period, unless the neighbor chooses a shorter one. It is never longer than the default.
    • A shorter period is chosen as a whole number of days, at least 1.
  • INV-CHK-7: A suspended neighbor can't check out a tool, and neither can a neighbor whose account is closed.
    • An account is suspended from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated, and closed for good from Neighbor Account Closed.
    • This also stops a suspended holder collecting a tool set aside for them. Their hold keeps its place, and the set-aside still lapses at the end of its collect-by date.
  • INV-CHK-8: There is no limit on how many tools one neighbor can have checked out at once.
  • INV-CHK-9: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The tool is then on loan, so it is not set aside for anyone, and the next hold waits for its return. When the tool comes back, the former holder is no longer in the queue.
    • The hold's end is recorded as Hold Collected by the Hold Collector (Collect Hold), which reacts to the checkout through Holds To Collect. The views that show holds end it from that event; this slice records nothing about the hold.
  • INV-CHK-11: The tool must have been added, and the borrower must be a registered account.
  • INV-CHK-12: Checking out with a loan ID that is already used opens no new loan.
    • A repeat with the same tool, borrower and loan period succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the loan since. A repeat with different details is refused.
    • The loan period compared is the one the loan started with: a request that leaves the period out is the same as one that sends the tool's default explicitly.

Check Out is offered on a reserved or set-aside tool to every neighbor, not only to the holder whose turn it is (Tool Catalog, INV-TCAT-11). This slice refuses anyone else with the reason (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-3a).

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: the cordless drill (tool D) has a 7-day default checkout period, Ana, Ben and Cara are registered, active neighbors with no overdue loans, and today is 5 October.

  • Happy path (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill from the Tool Catalog as loan L1, keeping the default period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for L1: the drill, Ana, a 7-day period, due 12 October, checked out today.
  • Shorter period chosen (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 3-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 3-day period, due 8 October.
  • Shortest period (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 1-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 1-day period, due 6 October.
  • Period equal to the default (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 7-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 7-day period, due 12 October.
  • Period longer than the default (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill with an 8-day period
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • Period of zero, or not whole (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill with a 0-day period, or a 2.5-day period
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • Tool already checked out (INV-CHK-2)
    • Given: Ben has the drill on loan
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with tool-checked-out: "This tool is already checked out." No event is recorded.
  • Retired tool (INV-CHK-4)
    • Given: the drill has been retired
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown tool (INV-CHK-11)
    • Given: no tool T9 has been added
    • When: Ana tries to check out T9
    • Then: refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-CHK-11)
    • Given: no account N9 has been registered
    • When: a request to check out the drill for N9 arrives
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't borrow tools while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana's account is closed
    • When: a request to check out the drill for Ana arrives
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Reinstated neighbor can borrow again (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has been reinstated, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • Overdue loan blocks a checkout (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, due 4 October, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with has-overdue-loan: "You have an overdue loan. Return it before borrowing another tool." No event is recorded.
  • A loan due today is not overdue (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, due 5 October, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • An extended loan is not overdue (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana's ladder loan was due 4 October, and Loan Extended moved it to 11 October
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • A loan ended by loss no longer blocks (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana's ladder loan was due 1 October, and Tool Lost has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • Several loans at once (INV-CHK-8)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder and the hedge trimmer on loan, neither overdue, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded. Ana now has three tools on loan.
  • Holder collects a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: Hold Fulfilled was recorded for Ben's hold on the drill with a collect-by date of 6 October, so the drill is set aside for him
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben, due 12 October. Nothing else is recorded; the Hold Collector then records Hold Collected for Ben's hold.
  • Holder collects on the collect-by date (INV-CHK-3)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, to collect by 5 October
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben.
  • Someone else tries to take a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-3)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, to collect by 6 October
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with set-aside-for-another: "This tool is set aside for another neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Overdue holder can't collect (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, and Ben has the ladder on loan, due 2 October
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with has-overdue-loan. The drill stays set aside for Ben until his collect-by date ends.
  • Suspended holder can't collect (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, and Ben is suspended
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended. His hold keeps its place.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned, Ben's hold is at the front of its queue and Cara's is behind it, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Ben checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben. Ben's hold ends without ever being fulfilled, by the Hold Collected the collector then records.
  • An early collector is out of the queue when the tool returns (INV-CHK-9, INV-CHK-3a)
    • Given: Ben checked out the drill as the front holder before his hold was fulfilled, with Cara's hold behind his. He has since returned it, and Cara's hold is still waiting.
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill again
    • Then: refused with reserved-for-another: "This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue." No event is recorded. Cara is now at the front.
  • Someone who isn't next tries to take a reserved tool (INV-CHK-3a)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned, with Ben's hold at the front and Cara's behind it, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Cara tries to check out the drill, and then Ana does
    • Then: both are refused with reserved-for-another: "This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue." No event is recorded.
  • Holder too late, another hold waiting (INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben on 14 October, to collect by 17 October, and Cara's hold is waiting. Hold Expired has not yet been recorded.
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: refused with pickup-window-ended: "Your pickup window has ended, and this tool has passed to the next neighbor in the queue." No event is recorded. Cara can check the drill out.
  • Someone else tries a lapsed set-aside while a hold waits (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: as above, on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded
    • When: Ana, who has no hold on the drill, tries to check it out
    • Then: refused with reserved-for-another. No event is recorded.
  • Next holder takes a lapsed set-aside before the expiry is recorded (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: as above, on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded
    • When: Cara checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Cara; the collector then records Hold Collected for her hold. Ben's hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • Lapsed set-aside, no hold waiting, taken by someone else (INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben, to collect by 17 October, no other hold is waiting, and Hold Expired has not yet been recorded
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana. Ben's hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • Lapsed set-aside, no hold waiting, taken by the former holder (INV-CHK-3b, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: as above
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben. His own checkout ends his hold, so no Hold Expired follows for it.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CHK-12)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: the drill, Ana, default period
    • When: the same Check Out Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. Ana still has one loan of the drill.
  • A loan ID reused for different details (INV-CHK-12)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: the drill, Ana
    • When: a Check Out Tool request for L1 arrives naming the ladder
    • Then: refused with loan-id-in-use: "That loan ID is already used by another loan." No event is recorded.
  • Someone checks out a tool for another neighbor (INV-CHK-1)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: a request to check out the drill for Ana comes from someone other than Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only check out tools for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • No sign-in (INV-CHK-1)
    • Given: a caller with no sign-in
    • When: they ask to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the Tool Catalog screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in, then requester-mismatch (INV-CHK-1).
  2. The loan ID is already used (INV-CHK-12): a repeat with the same details succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise loan-id-in-use.
  3. tool-not-found, then neighbor-not-found (INV-CHK-11).
  4. tool-retired (INV-CHK-4).
  5. tool-checked-out (INV-CHK-2).
  6. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-CHK-7).
  7. has-overdue-loan (INV-CHK-5).
  8. The tool's holds (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b):
    • set-aside-for-another: the tool is set aside and its collect-by date hasn't ended, and the requester isn't the holder.
    • pickup-window-ended: the set-aside's collect-by date has ended, another hold is waiting, and the requester is the former holder.
    • reserved-for-another: the tool is back with a hold waiting (or a lapsed set-aside with one waiting), and the requester isn't the neighbor at the front of the queue. This includes a third neighbor after a set-aside lapses.
  9. period-out-of-range (INV-CHK-6).
ReasonSentenceRule
loan-id-in-useThat loan ID is already used by another loan.INV-CHK-12
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-CHK-1
requester-mismatchYou can only check out tools for yourself.INV-CHK-1
tool-not-foundThere is no such tool.INV-CHK-11
neighbor-not-foundThere is no such neighbor.INV-CHK-11
tool-retiredThis tool has been retired.INV-CHK-4
tool-checked-outThis tool is already checked out.INV-CHK-2
account-closedThis account is closed.INV-CHK-7
neighbor-suspendedYou can't borrow tools while your account is suspended.INV-CHK-7
has-overdue-loanYou have an overdue loan. Return it before borrowing another tool.INV-CHK-5
set-aside-for-anotherThis tool is set aside for another neighbor.INV-CHK-3
pickup-window-endedYour pickup window has ended, and this tool has passed to the next neighbor in the queue.INV-CHK-3b
reserved-for-anotherThis tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue.INV-CHK-3a
period-out-of-rangeThe loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period.INV-CHK-6

loan-id-in-use, tool-not-found and neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same loan ID and the same tool, borrower and requested period succeeds and records nothing new, even if the loan has since been extended, returned or lost. So a retry after a lost response never opens a second loan.

Two neighbors checking out the same tool at the same moment: only one Tool Checked Out is recorded for the tool. The other request is refused with tool-checked-out, because each checkout is decided against the tool's loans as already recorded, one at a time.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may check out a tool only for themselves (INV-CHK-1); the shed manager doesn't check tools out. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; requester-mismatch means it isn't the neighborId in the request.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Checked Out links a neighbor to a tool and a due date. It holds no name or email; those stay on Neighbor Registered and Neighbor Email Changed.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Checked Out (this slice): loanId, toolId, neighborId, loanPeriodDays, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor), Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId. Queue order is the order these events were recorded.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, tool-inventory.md, tool-catalog.md and register-neighbor.md. Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate is the Date the fulfiller records (set by the system, as dueDate is on loans). Those slices aren't yet written in depth, and each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Neighbors To Flag. Extend Loan, Return Tool and Record Tool Lost act on the loan by its loan ID.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded; Check Out Tool no longer feeds the merged Neighbors view, Return Tool does (2026-11-01)

Slice: My Loans

Step 4 of 12 in Borrow and return a tool · after Tool Catalog — checked out · before Extend Loan · State View

Intent

Shows a neighbor the tools they have out right now, when each is due back, and anything that stands in the way of keeping a tool longer: the loan is overdue, someone else is waiting for the tool, or the tool has been retired. It also shows whether an overdue notice was sent or couldn't be delivered. It is the screen the neighbor extends and returns loans from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Loans screen.
  • Whose loans it shows: the loans of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Return (Return Tool slice) — offered on every listed loan (INV-MYL-12).
    • Extend (Extend Loan slice) — offered while canExtend is yes (INV-MYL-9, INV-MYL-10).

Read Model / View

  • View: My Loans built from events: "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Hold Placed", "Hold Cancelled", "Overdue Notice Sent", "Overdue Notice Failed", "Tool Returned", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the My Loans screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). overdue is worked out when the view is read, from dueDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Extend Loan and Return Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per open loan. ToolId, LoanId, HoldId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
loanIdLoanIdTool Checked Out.loanId.
neighborIdNeighborIdTool Checked Out.neighborId: the borrower.
toolIdToolIdTool Checked Out.toolId.
toolNameTextTool Checked Out.toolName.
checkedOutAtInstantTool Checked Out.checkedOutAt. Shown as the checkout date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.
dueDateDateTool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for this loan.
overdueBoolDerived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate (INV-MYL-4). Worked out when the view is read.
overdueNoticeTextOne of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for this loan, undelivered once Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYL-5).
holdWaitingBoolDerived: yes while at least one hold on toolId is waiting (INV-MYL-9). See the hold rules below.
toolRetiredBoolDerived: yes once Tool Retired is recorded for toolId (INV-MYL-10).
canExtendBoolDerived: yes unless overdue, holdWaiting or toolRetired is yes (INV-MYL-9, INV-MYL-10). Worked out when the view is read, because overdue is.

Hold rules. A hold on the loan's tool is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. This view doesn't hear Hold Fulfilled, and doesn't need to: a tool out on loan has no fulfilled hold, except in the brief gap described under Alternate & Error Flows. So here a hold counts as waiting from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when:

  • Hold Cancelled is recorded for it;
  • Hold Expired is recorded for it;

A hold held by the loan's own borrower never counts as waiting on that loan: it is the hold they collected by this checkout, and the Hold Collector ends it (Collect Hold). This view needn't hear Hold Collected for that.

Retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each end holds by recording Hold Cancelled for them (Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost, Close Account). This view hears only the Holds events for holds.

Holds placed before the loan began count the same as holds placed during it. To apply these rules, the view keeps, for each tool, the hold ID and holder of each hold that hasn't ended. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and is never returned.

Queries

  • List my loans. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every open loan whose borrower is that neighbor, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's loans (INV-MYL-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no open loans gets an empty list. Loans are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the loan was checked out (checkedOutAt); loans checked out at the same instant keep the order their Tool Checked Out was recorded (INV-MYL-13).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-MYL-1: A neighbor's My Loans shows only that neighbor's own loans.
    • The query returns only loans whose borrower is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else has a tool or who is waiting for one. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYL-2: Every checkout appears on the borrower's My Loans as one loan, with the tool and its due date.
    • The due date is the one Tool Checked Out carries. How it is set is Check Out Tool's rule.
    • A holder collecting a tool set aside for them is an ordinary checkout and appears the same way.
  • INV-MYL-3: When a loan is extended, its due date on My Loans becomes the extended due date.
    • The new due date is the one Loan Extended carries. How far an extension moves it is Extend Loan's rule (INV-EXT-3).
  • INV-MYL-4: A loan shows as overdue from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, and not before.
    • Overdue is worked out by comparing the due date with today. No event marks a loan overdue, so the screen shows it overdue on the day after the due date with nothing recorded.
    • An overdue loan can't be extended (INV-EXT-5, Extend Loan), so once a loan is overdue it stays overdue until it ends.
  • INV-MYL-5: Once an overdue notice is sent for a loan, My Loans shows that the borrower was notified.
    • If the notice later fails to deliver, My Loans shows instead that the overdue notice couldn't be delivered.
  • INV-MYL-6: A returned loan drops off My Loans, and so does a loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost.
    • My Loans shows only what the neighbor has out now. It keeps no borrowing history.
  • INV-MYL-7: Each loan shows the tool, the checkout date, the due date, whether it is overdue, and whether an overdue notice has been sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • There is no "due soon" state. Overdue is the only state a loan shows besides on loan.
  • INV-MYL-8: A loan's entry changes only through its own checkout, extension, overdue notice, return or loss, and through holds starting or ending on its tool.
    • That is: Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Overdue Notice Sent, Overdue Notice Failed, Tool Returned, Tool Lost, Hold Placed, Hold Cancelled, Hold Expired and Tool Retired.
    • The tool's name comes with Tool Checked Out.
  • INV-MYL-9: While any hold is waiting on a loan's tool, My Loans shows that the loan can't be extended because someone is waiting.
    • A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires; a tool retired or recorded lost, and a holder closing their account, end holds by recording Hold Cancelled. The borrower's own hold on the tool never counts (it is being collected). A tool on loan has no fulfilled hold, so for a loan's tool a hold waits until it ends.
    • This includes holds that were already waiting when the loan began. When no hold is waiting any more, the loan can be extended again.
  • INV-MYL-10: An overdue loan, and a loan whose tool has been retired, are marked as not extendable.
    • A tool can be retired while it is on loan. The loan stays on My Loans until it is returned or the tool is recorded lost, like any other loan.
    • Suspension is not shown on My Loans. A suspended neighbor sees it on My Account, and Extend Loan refuses an extension they try with its own reason (INV-EXT-7, Extend Loan).
  • INV-MYL-11: Applying the same event twice leaves My Loans as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYL-12: My Loans offers Return on every loan it lists, because Return Tool accepts a return for every open loan.
    • That includes overdue loans (INV-RET-5), loans of a suspended neighbor (INV-RET-7) and loans whose tool has been retired (INV-RET-9). The screen offers the action; nothing in this slice's view or query decides it, and Return Tool, not My Loans, is where a return is refused.
  • INV-MYL-13: Loans are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were checked out.
  • INV-MYL-14: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYL-15: My Loans is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool checked out (INV-MYL-2, INV-MYL-7, INV-MYL-12)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has no loans, and the cordless drill (T1) has no holds
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded at 10:00 on 5 October, shed time, for loan L1: Ana borrowing the drill, due 12 October
    • Then: Ana's My Loans lists L1: "Cordless drill", checked out 5 October, due 12 October, not overdue, overdue notice none, no hold waiting, extendable, with Return offered.
  • Loan extended (INV-MYL-3)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for L1, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: Ana's My Loans lists L1 due 19 October.
  • Not overdue on the due date (INV-MYL-4)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October
    • When: the list is read at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is not overdue, and is extendable.
  • Loan becomes overdue (INV-MYL-4, INV-MYL-10)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October, and the drill hasn't been returned
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 shows as overdue and not extendable. Nothing is recorded.
  • Overdue notice sent (INV-MYL-5)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans shows L1 as overdue, overdue notice none
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 shows overdue notice sent.
  • Overdue notice couldn't be delivered (INV-MYL-5)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans shows L1 with overdue notice sent
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 shows overdue notice undelivered.
  • Tool returned (INV-MYL-6)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1 (the drill) and L2 (a ladder)
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 drops off Ana's My Loans, and L2 is unchanged.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYL-6)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L2, overdue
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L2
    • Then: L2 drops off Ana's My Loans.
  • Someone places a hold on the borrowed tool (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October, with no hold waiting
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on the drill
    • Then: L1 shows a hold waiting and is not extendable. It doesn't say who is waiting.
  • One of two holds is cancelled (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from Ben's hold H1 and Cara's hold H2
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: L1 still shows a hold waiting, because H2 is.
  • The last waiting hold is cancelled (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from H2 only
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H2
    • Then: L1 shows no hold waiting and is extendable again.
  • The waiting holder closes their account (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from Ben's hold H1 only
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, because Ben closed his account
    • Then: L1 shows no hold waiting.
  • Tool retired while on loan (INV-MYL-9, INV-MYL-10, INV-MYL-12)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from Ben's hold H1, due 12 October
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill, with Hold Cancelled for H1
    • Then: L1 is still listed, due 12 October, with the tool retired, no hold waiting, not extendable, and Return still offered.
  • Loan starts with a hold already waiting (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: the drill was returned with Ben's hold H1 at position 1 and Cara's hold H2 at position 2, and it was set aside for Ben
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for loan L3: Ben collecting the drill
    • Then: H1 ends with Ben's checkout. Ben's My Loans lists L3 with a hold waiting, from H2, and not extendable.
  • Next loan after an expired hold (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: Ben's hold H1 on the drill was set aside for him and then Hold Expired was recorded for it. No other hold is waiting.
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for loan L4: Dan borrowing the drill
    • Then: Dan's My Loans lists L4 with no hold waiting, and extendable.
  • Other neighbors' loans (INV-MYL-1)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for loan L5: Ben borrowing a ladder
    • Then: Ben's My Loans lists L5, and Ana's My Loans is unchanged. Listing Ana's loans never returns L5.
  • Unrelated events don't change it (INV-MYL-8)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1 (the drill, T1), due 12 October, with no hold waiting
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana, and Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold on the ladder (T2)
    • Then: L1 is unchanged: still due 12 October, no hold waiting, extendable.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYL-11)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1 once
    • When: the same Tool Checked Out for L1 is applied again
    • Then: Ana's My Loans still lists L1 once, unchanged.
  • List order (INV-MYL-13)
    • Given: Ana checked out a ladder on 3 October, then a cordless drill on 5 October
    • When: her loans are listed
    • Then: the cordless drill comes first, then the ladder.
  • No loans (INV-MYL-1)
    • Given: Ana has no open loans
    • When: her loans are listed
    • Then: the list is empty.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYL-14)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Loans is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYL-15)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the loans of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own loans." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYL-14).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYL-15).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-MYL-14
requester-mismatchYou can only see your own loans.INV-MYL-15
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYL-11). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a loan that has ended: once a loan is returned or its tool recorded lost, it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or an Overdue Notice Failed that arrives after the loan ended) changes nothing.
  • A lapsed set-aside that hasn't expired yet: after a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, someone else may check the tool out before Hold Expired is recorded for the lapsed hold. This view doesn't hear Hold Fulfilled, so until Hold Expired lands it counts that hold as waiting, and the new loan briefly shows a hold waiting. It clears when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, Extend just as a hold is placed, or Return just as the shed manager records the tool lost). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own loans (INV-MYL-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYL-15), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYL-14).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own loans only. It never shows who holds or is waiting for a tool. The holders it keeps for matching hold events are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, checkedOutAt.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Overdue Notice Failed (Record Overdue Notice Failure): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end.
    • The loan and hold events' keys match slices/tool-inventory.md and slices/tool-catalog.md. checkedOutAt matches Check Out Tool (slices/check-out-tool.md). The other events are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Extend Loan and Return Tool.

Open Questions

  • INV-MYL-12 (Return offered on every loan) has no enforcement site in this slice; rephrase it to cite Return Tool's INV-RET-5/7/9, which it relies on, or drop it (conformance 2026-11-01, uncertainty) — v2: kept and rephrased to cite INV-RET-5/7/9 and say the screen, not the view, offers it (2026-11-01)

Slice: Extend Loan

Step 5 of 12 in Borrow and return a tool · after My Loans · before Tool Inventory — loan extended · State Change

Intent

Let a borrower keep a tool longer by extending their loan from My Loans. An extension moves the due date later by one of the tool's default checkout periods. It is refused while someone is waiting for the tool, once the loan is overdue, while the borrower is suspended, and once the tool has been retired.

Trigger & Actor

The borrower, from the My Loans screen, on one of their own loans that My Loans offers Extend on. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.

Command / Input

Command: Extend Loan

A LoanId is a UUID. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone. "Today" is that date at the moment the command is handled.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor extending, who must be the one making the request and the loan's borrower (INV-EXT-1).
loanIdLoanIdyesThe loan to extend. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-EXT-9).
fromDueDateDateyesThe due date the borrower is extending from, as My Loans showed it. Must be the loan's current due date, unless this exact extension has already been recorded (INV-EXT-10).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Loans @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Loan Extended → context Loans Read by: My Loans, Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the new due date shown); Overdue Loans To Notify and Neighbors To Flag (when the loan becomes overdue, and whether a return is late); Undelivered Notices and Flagged Neighbors (loan details shown there).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
loanIdLoanIdyesFrom the command.
fromDueDateDateyesFrom the command: the loan's due date before this extension.
dueDateDateyesSet by the system: the new due date, fromDueDate plus the tool's default checkout period (INV-EXT-3).
extendedAtInstantyesThe UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

A later extension records a new Loan Extended; this one never changes. A loan's current due date is the dueDate of its latest Loan Extended, or of its Tool Checked Out if it has never been extended.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Loan Extended moves the loan's due date in My Loans, Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog, and in the lists that work out overdue loans and late returns. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-EXT-1: Only the borrower can extend a loan, and they do it themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId. The request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch), and the loan must be theirs: the neighbor who checked the tool out (not-your-loan). Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in, before anything else is checked.
  • INV-EXT-2: Only an open loan can be extended.
    • A loan is open from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan.
  • INV-EXT-3: An extension adds one of the tool's default checkout periods to the loan's current due date.
    • It adds the tool's default period even if the borrower chose a shorter period at checkout.
    • The default period is the one on Tool Added. It never changes.
  • INV-EXT-4: An extension is refused while any hold is waiting on the tool.
    • A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account. This is the meaning the Tool Catalog and Place Hold use.
    • My Loans shows the same (INV-MYL-9), except for a moment it can't see: when a lapsed set-aside has gone to the next holder and its Hold Expired isn't recorded yet. My Loans then holds back Extend for a few seconds; this slice already allows it.
    • Holds that were already waiting when the loan began count too.
  • INV-EXT-5: An extension is refused once the loan is overdue.
    • A loan is overdue from the start of the day after its current due date, in the shed's local time. On the due date itself, the loan can still be extended.
    • Only the overdue loan itself is refused. The same borrower can still extend their other loans that are not overdue.
  • INV-EXT-6: There is no limit on how many times a loan can be extended, as long as each extension meets the other rules here.
  • INV-EXT-7: A suspended neighbor can't extend a loan.
    • A neighbor is suspended from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated. Once reinstated, they can extend again.
    • A closed account has no open loans, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan, so it needs no rule here.
  • INV-EXT-8: A loan whose tool has been retired can't be extended.
    • The loan carries on until the tool is returned or recorded lost.
  • INV-EXT-9: The loan must exist.
  • INV-EXT-10: Extending from a due date that has already been extended from adds nothing.
    • A repeated request succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the loan since. A request whose fromDueDate is neither the loan's current due date nor one it has already been extended from is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana has the cordless drill on loan L1. The drill has a 7-day default checkout period. L1 is due 12 October, has never been extended, and no hold is waiting on the drill. Ana is active, and today is 10 October.

  • Happy path (INV-EXT-3)
    • Given: L1 as above
    • When: Ana extends L1 from My Loans, from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded for L1, from 12 October to 19 October.
  • Extending on the due date (INV-EXT-5)
    • Given: today is 12 October
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 19 October.
  • Extending the day after the due date (INV-EXT-5)
    • Given: today is 13 October, and L1 is still due 12 October
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1 from 12 October
    • Then: refused with loan-overdue: "This loan is overdue and can't be extended. Please return the tool." No event is recorded.
  • Extending again (INV-EXT-6)
    • Given: L1 has already been extended once and is due 19 October; today is 18 October
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 19 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, from 19 October to 26 October.
  • Extending a loan checked out for a shorter period (INV-EXT-3)
    • Given: Ana checked out the drill for 3 days, so L1 is due 8 October; today is 7 October
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 8 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 15 October: the drill's 7-day default, not 3 days.
  • A hold is waiting (INV-EXT-4)
    • Given: Ben has placed a hold on the drill, and it is still waiting
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with hold-waiting: "Someone is waiting for this tool, so this loan can't be extended." No event is recorded.
  • A hold was waiting when the loan began (INV-EXT-4)
    • Given: Ana checked out the drill as the front holder, and Cara's hold was behind hers and is still waiting
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with hold-waiting.
  • The waiting hold has ended (INV-EXT-4)
    • Given: Ben placed a hold on the drill, and then cancelled it
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 19 October.
  • Another of the borrower's loans is overdue (INV-EXT-5)
    • Given: Ana also has the ladder on loan, due 4 October, so it is overdue
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded for L1, to 19 October. The ladder loan is still overdue.
  • Suspended borrower (INV-EXT-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't extend loans while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Reinstated borrower (INV-EXT-7)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has been reinstated
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 19 October.
  • Tool retired while on loan (INV-EXT-8)
    • Given: the drill was retired while Ana has it on loan
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired, so this loan can't be extended. Please return it by the due date." No event is recorded.
  • Loan already returned (INV-EXT-2)
    • Given: Ana has returned the drill, ending L1
    • When: a request to extend L1 from 12 October arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Loan ended by loss (INV-EXT-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost has been recorded for L1
    • When: a request to extend L1 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-ended.
  • Unknown loan (INV-EXT-9)
    • Given: no loan L9 has been checked out
    • When: a request to extend L9 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's loan (INV-EXT-1)
    • Given: L1 is Ana's loan
    • When: Ben, naming himself, tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with not-your-loan: "You can only extend your own loans." No event is recorded.
  • A request that doesn't come from the neighbor it names (INV-EXT-1)
    • Given: L1 is Ana's loan
    • When: a request to extend L1, naming Ana, comes from someone other than Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only extend loans for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-EXT-10)
    • Given: Loan Extended was recorded for L1, from 12 October to 19 October
    • When: the same request to extend L1 from 12 October arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. L1 is still due 19 October.
  • The same request after a hold was placed (INV-EXT-10)
    • Given: Loan Extended was recorded for L1, from 12 October to 19 October, and Ben has since placed a hold on the drill
    • When: the same request to extend L1 from 12 October arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Extending from a due date that isn't current (INV-EXT-10)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October and has never been extended
    • When: a request to extend L1 from 5 October arrives
    • Then: refused with due-date-changed: "This loan's due date has changed. Check it and try again." No event is recorded.
  • No sign-in (INV-EXT-1)
    • Given: a caller with no sign-in
    • When: they ask to extend L1
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the borrower on the My Loans screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in, then requester-mismatch (INV-EXT-1).
  2. loan-not-found (INV-EXT-9).
  3. not-your-loan (INV-EXT-1).
  4. If a Loan Extended for this loan already has the same fromDueDate, the request is a repeat: it succeeds and records nothing (INV-EXT-10).
  5. loan-ended (INV-EXT-2).
  6. due-date-changed, if fromDueDate isn't the loan's current due date (INV-EXT-10).
  7. neighbor-suspended (INV-EXT-7).
  8. tool-retired (INV-EXT-8).
  9. loan-overdue (INV-EXT-5).
  10. hold-waiting (INV-EXT-4).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-EXT-1
requester-mismatchYou can only extend loans for yourself.INV-EXT-1
loan-not-foundThere is no such loan.INV-EXT-9
not-your-loanYou can only extend your own loans.INV-EXT-1
loan-endedThis loan has ended.INV-EXT-2
due-date-changedThis loan's due date has changed. Check it and try again.INV-EXT-10
neighbor-suspendedYou can't extend loans while your account is suspended.INV-EXT-7
tool-retiredThis tool has been retired, so this loan can't be extended. Please return it by the due date.INV-EXT-8
loan-overdueThis loan is overdue and can't be extended. Please return the tool.INV-EXT-5
hold-waitingSomeone is waiting for this tool, so this loan can't be extended.INV-EXT-4

loan-not-found and requester-mismatch can only come from a faulty or impersonating caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed loan ID (not a UUID), or a fromDueDate that isn't a date, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: each extension is identified by the loan and the due date it extends from. A double submit, or a retry after a lost response, carries the same fromDueDate, so it succeeds with nothing recorded, even if the loan has since changed. It never extends the loan twice.

Two requests for the same loan at the same moment: each is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time, so only one Loan Extended is recorded from a given due date.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the borrower may extend their own loan (INV-EXT-1). The shed manager doesn't extend loans. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.
  • PII & compliance: Loan Extended holds only the loan and its dates. No name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, checkedOutAt.
    • Loan Extended (this slice): loanId, fromDueDate, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold), Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, check-out-tool.md, tool-inventory.md and tool-catalog.md. This slice adds fromDueDate and extendedAt to Loan Extended; readers that only need the new due date keep reading {loanId, dueDate}.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans, Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, Overdue Loans To Notify, Neighbors To Flag, Undelivered Notices and Flagged Neighbors (the new due date).

Open Questions

None.

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v1: v1 keeps the old view names in prose; the views named no longer exist in the model; deferred to v2 (2026-11-01, Mike Key)

Slice: My Loans

Step 4 of 12 in Borrow and return a tool · after Tool Catalog — checked out · before Extend Loan · State View

Intent

Shows a neighbor the tools they have out right now, when each is due back, and anything that stands in the way of keeping a tool longer: the loan is overdue, someone else is waiting for the tool, or the tool has been retired. It also shows whether an overdue notice was sent or couldn't be delivered. It is the screen the neighbor extends and returns loans from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Loans screen.
  • Whose loans it shows: the loans of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Return (Return Tool slice) — offered on every listed loan (INV-MYL-12).
    • Extend (Extend Loan slice) — offered while canExtend is yes (INV-MYL-9, INV-MYL-10).

Read Model / View

  • View: My Loans built from events: "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Hold Placed", "Hold Cancelled", "Overdue Notice Sent", "Overdue Notice Failed", "Tool Returned", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the My Loans screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). overdue is worked out when the view is read, from dueDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Extend Loan and Return Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per open loan. ToolId, LoanId, HoldId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
loanIdLoanIdTool Checked Out.loanId.
neighborIdNeighborIdTool Checked Out.neighborId: the borrower.
toolIdToolIdTool Checked Out.toolId.
toolNameTextTool Checked Out.toolName.
checkedOutAtInstantTool Checked Out.checkedOutAt. Shown as the checkout date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.
dueDateDateTool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for this loan.
overdueBoolDerived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate (INV-MYL-4). Worked out when the view is read.
overdueNoticeTextOne of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for this loan, undelivered once Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYL-5).
holdWaitingBoolDerived: yes while at least one hold on toolId is waiting (INV-MYL-9). See the hold rules below.
toolRetiredBoolDerived: yes once Tool Retired is recorded for toolId (INV-MYL-10).
canExtendBoolDerived: yes unless overdue, holdWaiting or toolRetired is yes (INV-MYL-9, INV-MYL-10). Worked out when the view is read, because overdue is.

Hold rules. A hold on the loan's tool is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. This view doesn't hear Hold Fulfilled, and doesn't need to: a tool out on loan has no fulfilled hold, except in the brief gap described under Alternate & Error Flows. So here a hold counts as waiting from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when:

  • Hold Cancelled is recorded for it;
  • Hold Expired is recorded for it;

A hold held by the loan's own borrower never counts as waiting on that loan: it is the hold they collected by this checkout, and the Hold Collector ends it (Collect Hold). This view needn't hear Hold Collected for that.

Retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each end holds by recording Hold Cancelled for them (Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost, Close Account). This view hears only the Holds events for holds.

Holds placed before the loan began count the same as holds placed during it. To apply these rules, the view keeps, for each tool, the hold ID and holder of each hold that hasn't ended. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and is never returned.

Queries

  • List my loans. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every open loan whose borrower is that neighbor, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's loans (INV-MYL-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no open loans gets an empty list. Loans are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the loan was checked out (checkedOutAt); loans checked out at the same instant keep the order their Tool Checked Out was recorded (INV-MYL-13).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-MYL-1: A neighbor's My Loans shows only that neighbor's own loans.
    • The query returns only loans whose borrower is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else has a tool or who is waiting for one. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYL-2: Every checkout appears on the borrower's My Loans as one loan, with the tool and its due date.
    • The due date is the one Tool Checked Out carries. How it is set is Check Out Tool's rule.
    • A holder collecting a tool set aside for them is an ordinary checkout and appears the same way.
  • INV-MYL-3: When a loan is extended, its due date on My Loans becomes the extended due date.
    • The new due date is the one Loan Extended carries. How far an extension moves it is Extend Loan's rule (INV-EXT-3).
  • INV-MYL-4: A loan shows as overdue from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, and not before.
    • Overdue is worked out by comparing the due date with today. No event marks a loan overdue, so the screen shows it overdue on the day after the due date with nothing recorded.
    • An overdue loan can't be extended (INV-EXT-5, Extend Loan), so once a loan is overdue it stays overdue until it ends.
  • INV-MYL-5: Once an overdue notice is sent for a loan, My Loans shows that the borrower was notified.
    • If the notice later fails to deliver, My Loans shows instead that the overdue notice couldn't be delivered.
  • INV-MYL-6: A returned loan drops off My Loans, and so does a loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost.
    • My Loans shows only what the neighbor has out now. It keeps no borrowing history.
  • INV-MYL-7: Each loan shows the tool, the checkout date, the due date, whether it is overdue, and whether an overdue notice has been sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • There is no "due soon" state. Overdue is the only state a loan shows besides on loan.
  • INV-MYL-8: A loan's entry changes only through its own checkout, extension, overdue notice, return or loss, and through holds starting or ending on its tool.
    • That is: Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Overdue Notice Sent, Overdue Notice Failed, Tool Returned, Tool Lost, Hold Placed, Hold Cancelled, Hold Expired and Tool Retired.
    • The tool's name comes with Tool Checked Out.
  • INV-MYL-9: While any hold is waiting on a loan's tool, My Loans shows that the loan can't be extended because someone is waiting.
    • A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires; a tool retired or recorded lost, and a holder closing their account, end holds by recording Hold Cancelled. The borrower's own hold on the tool never counts (it is being collected). A tool on loan has no fulfilled hold, so for a loan's tool a hold waits until it ends.
    • This includes holds that were already waiting when the loan began. When no hold is waiting any more, the loan can be extended again.
  • INV-MYL-10: An overdue loan, and a loan whose tool has been retired, are marked as not extendable.
    • A tool can be retired while it is on loan. The loan stays on My Loans until it is returned or the tool is recorded lost, like any other loan.
    • Suspension is not shown on My Loans. A suspended neighbor sees it on My Account, and Extend Loan refuses an extension they try with its own reason (INV-EXT-7, Extend Loan).
  • INV-MYL-11: Applying the same event twice leaves My Loans as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYL-12: My Loans offers Return on every loan it lists, because Return Tool accepts a return for every open loan.
    • That includes overdue loans (INV-RET-5), loans of a suspended neighbor (INV-RET-7) and loans whose tool has been retired (INV-RET-9). The screen offers the action; nothing in this slice's view or query decides it, and Return Tool, not My Loans, is where a return is refused.
  • INV-MYL-13: Loans are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were checked out.
  • INV-MYL-14: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYL-15: My Loans is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool checked out (INV-MYL-2, INV-MYL-7, INV-MYL-12)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has no loans, and the cordless drill (T1) has no holds
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded at 10:00 on 5 October, shed time, for loan L1: Ana borrowing the drill, due 12 October
    • Then: Ana's My Loans lists L1: "Cordless drill", checked out 5 October, due 12 October, not overdue, overdue notice none, no hold waiting, extendable, with Return offered.
  • Loan extended (INV-MYL-3)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for L1, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: Ana's My Loans lists L1 due 19 October.
  • Not overdue on the due date (INV-MYL-4)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October
    • When: the list is read at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is not overdue, and is extendable.
  • Loan becomes overdue (INV-MYL-4, INV-MYL-10)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October, and the drill hasn't been returned
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 shows as overdue and not extendable. Nothing is recorded.
  • Overdue notice sent (INV-MYL-5)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans shows L1 as overdue, overdue notice none
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 shows overdue notice sent.
  • Overdue notice couldn't be delivered (INV-MYL-5)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans shows L1 with overdue notice sent
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 shows overdue notice undelivered.
  • Tool returned (INV-MYL-6)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1 (the drill) and L2 (a ladder)
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 drops off Ana's My Loans, and L2 is unchanged.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYL-6)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L2, overdue
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L2
    • Then: L2 drops off Ana's My Loans.
  • Someone places a hold on the borrowed tool (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1, due 12 October, with no hold waiting
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on the drill
    • Then: L1 shows a hold waiting and is not extendable. It doesn't say who is waiting.
  • One of two holds is cancelled (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from Ben's hold H1 and Cara's hold H2
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: L1 still shows a hold waiting, because H2 is.
  • The last waiting hold is cancelled (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from H2 only
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H2
    • Then: L1 shows no hold waiting and is extendable again.
  • The waiting holder closes their account (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from Ben's hold H1 only
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, because Ben closed his account
    • Then: L1 shows no hold waiting.
  • Tool retired while on loan (INV-MYL-9, INV-MYL-10, INV-MYL-12)
    • Given: L1 shows a hold waiting, from Ben's hold H1, due 12 October
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill, with Hold Cancelled for H1
    • Then: L1 is still listed, due 12 October, with the tool retired, no hold waiting, not extendable, and Return still offered.
  • Loan starts with a hold already waiting (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: the drill was returned with Ben's hold H1 at position 1 and Cara's hold H2 at position 2, and it was set aside for Ben
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for loan L3: Ben collecting the drill
    • Then: H1 ends with Ben's checkout. Ben's My Loans lists L3 with a hold waiting, from H2, and not extendable.
  • Next loan after an expired hold (INV-MYL-9)
    • Given: Ben's hold H1 on the drill was set aside for him and then Hold Expired was recorded for it. No other hold is waiting.
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for loan L4: Dan borrowing the drill
    • Then: Dan's My Loans lists L4 with no hold waiting, and extendable.
  • Other neighbors' loans (INV-MYL-1)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for loan L5: Ben borrowing a ladder
    • Then: Ben's My Loans lists L5, and Ana's My Loans is unchanged. Listing Ana's loans never returns L5.
  • Unrelated events don't change it (INV-MYL-8)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1 (the drill, T1), due 12 October, with no hold waiting
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana, and Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold on the ladder (T2)
    • Then: L1 is unchanged: still due 12 October, no hold waiting, extendable.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYL-11)
    • Given: Ana's My Loans lists L1 once
    • When: the same Tool Checked Out for L1 is applied again
    • Then: Ana's My Loans still lists L1 once, unchanged.
  • List order (INV-MYL-13)
    • Given: Ana checked out a ladder on 3 October, then a cordless drill on 5 October
    • When: her loans are listed
    • Then: the cordless drill comes first, then the ladder.
  • No loans (INV-MYL-1)
    • Given: Ana has no open loans
    • When: her loans are listed
    • Then: the list is empty.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYL-14)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Loans is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYL-15)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the loans of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own loans." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYL-14).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYL-15).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-MYL-14
requester-mismatchYou can only see your own loans.INV-MYL-15
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYL-11). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a loan that has ended: once a loan is returned or its tool recorded lost, it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or an Overdue Notice Failed that arrives after the loan ended) changes nothing.
  • A lapsed set-aside that hasn't expired yet: after a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, someone else may check the tool out before Hold Expired is recorded for the lapsed hold. This view doesn't hear Hold Fulfilled, so until Hold Expired lands it counts that hold as waiting, and the new loan briefly shows a hold waiting. It clears when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, Extend just as a hold is placed, or Return just as the shed manager records the tool lost). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own loans (INV-MYL-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYL-15), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYL-14).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own loans only. It never shows who holds or is waiting for a tool. The holders it keeps for matching hold events are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, checkedOutAt.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Overdue Notice Failed (Record Overdue Notice Failure): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end.
    • The loan and hold events' keys match slices/tool-inventory.md and slices/tool-catalog.md. checkedOutAt matches Check Out Tool (slices/check-out-tool.md). The other events are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Extend Loan and Return Tool.

Open Questions

  • INV-MYL-12 (Return offered on every loan) has no enforcement site in this slice; rephrase it to cite Return Tool's INV-RET-5/7/9, which it relies on, or drop it (conformance 2026-11-01, uncertainty) — v2: kept and rephrased to cite INV-RET-5/7/9 and say the screen, not the view, offers it (2026-11-01)
